title: How Adam Robinson grew RB2B to $6.7M ARR with a founder brand on LinkedIn
summary: Adam Robinson explains how RB2B started as a pivot from LinkedIn content, how a crude Slack mockup proved demand, and how he built a founder brand by repeating a few ideas. He also covers the risk of depending on one channel and the churn ceiling that pushes him to widen the product.

principles.text: Test a crude version fast: if people pay for something rough, pursue it.
principles.quote: if you give something to somebody that sucks and they pay you for it, that's like indicator one that you should probably pursue it.

principles.text: How data is presented can change demand dramatically; a Slack feed with headshots beat a spreadsheet of identical data.
principles.quote: the enthusiasm was like 11 out of 10 for the Slack thing and like 2 out of 10 for this other experience of of the same data, right?

principles.text: Products usually come from stumbling onto something that works better, not from audience-first planning.
principles.quote: you're kind of doing one thing that's working okay and then there's this other thing that you kind of stumble along that it's clear that it will work much better and so you like go all in on that

principles.text: Become known for something by repeating the same few ideas from many angles on every channel.
principles.quote: You say the same couple things over and over again in a thousand different ways on every single possible channel. And then you're the guy that is that, right?

principles.text: Reverse-engineer high-performing posts: map your story onto the structure of proven winners.
principles.quote: just kind of put them all in a row and like see the architecture of the post. See if you can put your story on that architecture

principles.text: Single-channel dependence is a risk; he is diversifying and widening the product because churn caps growth and extra features make it stickier.
principles.quote: you can beg people to not cancel and you'll maybe get 10% of them, but like you start building other stuff, and it just gets stickier.
